decisions.decision: A saved ticket with an invalid `due` value prevents startup even with `DUE_TIMES` off, and the load error identifies the record.
decisions.alternative: The service could continue serving with due times off and require operators to repair the affected record before enabling the feature.

decisions.decision: An explicitly empty `DUE_HOURS_*` variable selects the default for that priority.
decisions.alternative: An empty variable could be treated as a configuration error so a missing deployment value cannot silently set the wrong deadlines.

decisions.decision: Startup accepts an existing valid `due` as authoritative even when other tickets in the same file still need backfill.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted operators to verify prepopulated deadlines before the service accepts them as fixed commitments.

decisions.decision: Operators deploy with the switch off, verify that the data file contains due times, and then enable the feature in a separate step.
decisions.alternative: With `DUE_TIMES=on` already configured, the service could verify the completed write before exposing due times during the first deployment.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md, R-10 (line 71), and repo/docs/shiploop/environment.md, Access and accounts (line 31)

decisions.decision: Ticket notifications keep their existing content and are sent on the same events as before.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted the ticket receipt to tell users the response deadline the help desk is promising.

decisions.decision: When `overdue=true` is combined with both `status` and `priority`, an overdue ticket can match either of those two filters.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have expected the overdue listing to require both filters to match, as the existing API documentation describes for ticket lists.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md, R-5 combination (line 39), and repo/docs/api.md, List tickets (lines 76–77)

decisions.decision: The creation audit entry records only title, priority, requester and status, so the initial deadline is available on the ticket itself.
decisions.alternative: The creation audit entry could also record the original `due` so an operator can recover the deadline from history.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md, R-1 preserved behavior (line 11) and R-3 (line 25)

decisions.decision: Due times appear in HTTP ticket responses, while the operator CLI and weekly report keep their existing output even after activation.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted due times in the CLI’s human-readable views and overdue counts in the weekly report while preserving the raw columns used by scripts.
decisions.where: record/01-intake.md, Q6 (lines 115–121), and repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md, R-4, R-7 and R-9 (lines 29, 52 and 67)

decisions.decision: Migrated files still advertise format version 1 and carry `due` as an optional field on each ticket.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted a separate, backward-compatible migration marker so operators can identify a completed backfill without inspecting the tickets.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md, R-8 (lines 59–62), and record/03-research.md, Q1 result (line 16)

decisions.decision: A request body containing `due` receives a 400 unknown-field error, including when a client echoes the server’s deadline in a PATCH.
decisions.alternative: The API could accept and ignore `due` as a read-only response field so clients can echo it without changing the deadline.

decisions.decision: The overdue list filters before paging and returns matching tickets in ticket ID order with the usual `limit` and `cursor` behavior.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted the oldest missed deadline first so operators can use the first page to triage overdue tickets.

decisions.decision: Backfill preserves each ticket’s existing `updated` timestamp.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted backfill to advance `updated` so downstream consumers can detect the new deadline as a ticket change.
decisions.where: repo/docs/shiploop/spec.md, R-6 (lines 43 and 47), and record/01-intake.md, Q2 (line 82)

decisions.decision: The API represents `due` as an ISO 8601 UTC string in the same format as `created` and `updated`.
decisions.alternative: The requester might have wanted a numeric Unix timestamp for clients that compare deadlines directly.
The requester might have wanted a major version because activating the feature changes ticket payloads that strict API clients may validate.
